1.0: Cassian Andor, the thief from Ferrix who becomes one of the Rebellion's most capable agents and gives Andor its name, names the first release: the bridge, lights, scenes and zone lights that every later release builds on.
1.1: Brasso, Cassian's loyal friend on Ferrix who always looks out for him, names the release that brings Hue motion sensors and MotionAware areas into Control4: a dependable lookout in every room.
1.2: Taramyn Barcona, the former stormtrooper who drills the Aldhani heist crew into a disciplined unit, names the release that cuts the Hue Bridge from 29 actions to 9 and has it do its routine work by itself: finding bridges, re-linking replaced bulbs and keeping names in step.
1.3: Kerri, the younger sister Cassian lost when he left Kenari and goes looking for at the very start of the series, names the release that picks up where things left off: a motion hold cut short by a restart resumes for the rest of its time, and a held keypad button ramps lamp by lamp instead of jumping.
1.4: Maarva Andor, who raised Cassian on Ferrix and whose final message brings the whole town to a halt, names the release in which a tap brings a ramping light to a halt where it is, as on a Control4 dimmer.
1.5: Kenari, the jungle world where Cassian grew up before Maarva and Clem took him to Ferrix, names the release that makes Control4 the home of the house's lighting: it finds the automations living in the Hue bridge, turns lights on the way Control4 does, lets Hue lights join Control4 load groups and shows them offline when the bridge cannot be reached.
